current_clause.heading: Definition
current_clause.text:
Let an object be a finite disjoint union of smooth embedded circles in the oriented plane $\mathbb R^2$, including the empty union. A cobordism from $C_0$ to $C_1$ is a compact smooth orientable surface properly embedded in $\mathbb R^2\times[0,1]$, with boundary $C_0\times\{0\}\sqcup C_1\times\{1\}$, product collars at those boundaries, and no other boundary. Surfaces are identified up to ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars. Compose cobordisms by gluing along their common boundary circles; the identity of $C$ is $C\times[0,1]$, and disjoint union gives the monoidal product. Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be this additive monoidal category before imposing local relations.

Take the free abelian group on these isotopy classes of cobordisms and quotient by the following local relations, which are required to hold inside every surrounding cobordism. A sphere component is zero (the S relation). Adding a disjoint torus component multiplies a cobordism by $2$ (the T relation). For four disjoint disk patches numbered $1,2,3,4$, write $S_{ij}$ for the surface obtained by deleting the interiors of patches $i,j$ and joining their boundary circles by an orientable tube; the four-tube relation is $S_{12}+S_{34}=S_{13}+S_{24}$. The resulting additive monoidal category is denoted $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

current_clause.heading: Definition
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Let $K_0,K_1\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots. A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

current_clause.heading: Definition
Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be compact smooth properly embedded oriented surfaces from fixed oriented knots $K_0$ to $K_1$, with the same boundary parametrizations and product collars. Suppose their generic movies represent ambient isotopic cobordisms by an isotopy fixed on those collars. Then one movie can be changed to the other by a finite sequence of the fifteen Carter–Saito movie moves, sweep-around moves, and interchanges of two disjoint elementary movie events (including disjoint critical points of the surface-height function). A sweep-around moves a closing arc of a one-interval tangle over the tangle to its other side and back underneath, or reverses that movie; geometrically it is a local sheet passage through the missing vertical arc in a spatial chart $S^3\setminus\{\infty\}$. Every intermediate movie represents a generic surface cobordism with the same fixed boundary data.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be the additive monoidal category of oriented cobordisms before the S, T, and four-tube relations are imposed, and let $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$ be its quotient by those relations. Suppose $F:\mathsf{Cob}_3\to\mathsf{GrAb}$ is a symmetric monoidal functor to graded abelian groups and homogeneous maps, with a circle sent to $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, a cup to $\eta(1)=1$, a cap to $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, a merge pair of pants to $m$, and a split pair of pants to $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\ \Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. Then every sphere component is sent to zero, every disjoint torus component acts by multiplication by $2$, and the two sides of the four-tube relation induce the same map. Therefore $F$ factors through an additive monoidal functor on $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

current_clause.heading: Definition
current_clause.text:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with admissible Heegaard data and regular almost-complex structures for its elementary pieces. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For a piece represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{n_w(\phi)}V^{n_z(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ is the distinguished top-degree generator for the intermediate Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class, and the other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Let $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$ be a strongly admissible pointed Heegaard triple for a decorated knot cobordism, and fix one Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ and nonnegative $w,z$-multiplicities. For generic fixed almost-complex data compatible with the ends, the Maslov-index-zero triangle moduli spaces used in the triangle-count map are regular zero-manifolds and finite. For generic one-parameter families, the universal triangle moduli spaces are regular with the parameter included in the expected dimension; slice counts are taken at regular parameter values. The compactified one-dimensional Maslov-index-one triangle spaces have precisely the broken triangle/strip strata and the allowed boundary-degeneration strata; gluing supplies collars at broken ends. In a one-parameter family the compactified universal index-zero spaces additionally have the two parameter-endpoint strata; the zero-dimensional universal index-minus-one spaces define the homotopy terms. In the mod-two count, the stated exact boundary strata give the chain-map equation and the chain homotopies required when the auxiliary data vary. No additional ends arise from sphere bubbling, escape through nonzero periodic domains, or uncontrolled marked-point multiplicities.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. If the decorated cobordism is a composite of $(W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1)$ followed by $(W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2)$, then for fixed Spin-c structures $\mathfrak s_i$ on $W_i$,
$$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element, so the sum has one term and the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy.

current_clause.heading: Definition
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice and fix a generic movie $M$ of a smooth oriented surface cobordism $\Sigma$ from an oriented link $L_0$ to an oriented link $L_1$. For each regular frame $D$, let $Kh(D)$ be the normalized integral Khovanov homology group. Associate to a birth the unit map $\eta:\mathbb Z\to\mathcal A$, $\eta(1)=1$; associate to a death the counit $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathbb Z$, $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$; and associate to a saddle the multiplication $m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ when two resolution circles merge, or the comultiplication $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ when one splits. Each local map is tensored with the identity on unaffected circles. Associate to planar isotopy the induced identification of the cube complexes, and to a Reidemeister move the specified local normalized chain homotopy equivalence from the signed unit/counit and Gaussian-cancellation models, with its specified inverse in the reverse direction. Use the fixed local orientation cases and the Koszul crossing-order correction $(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$ when crossings $a,b$ are interchanged. These local maps are chosen once; composing them with an arbitrary automorphism of a complex is not an allowed change of representative. Compose the induced maps on homology in movie order and denote the result by $Kh(M):Kh(L_0)\to Kh(L_1)$, considered modulo multiplication by $-1$. This definition fixes a movie; independence from changing the movie is not included in the definition.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. For each Carter–Saito movie move, the two movie segments have the same incoming and outgoing oriented link diagrams and represent isotopic portions of an oriented surface cobordism relative to their boundary collars. The induced maps on the integral even Khovanov homology groups of those diagrams differ by multiplication by a single overall sign. The same conclusion holds when two disjoint critical points of the height function are interchanged.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text:
Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented cobordism from an oriented knot $K_0$ to an oriented knot $K_1$, with fixed product collars and fixed endpoint diagrams. Every generic movie $M$ of $\Sigma$ defines a map of bidegree $(0,\chi(\Sigma))$,
$$
Kh(M):Kh^{i,j}(K_0)\longrightarrow Kh^{i,j+\chi(\Sigma)}(K_1),
$$
where $\chi(\Sigma)$ is the Euler characteristic of the surface and the integral even Khovanov groups use the normalized crossing shifts. If two such movies represent cobordisms related by an ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars, their maps differ by multiplication by a single overall sign, independent of the input class. The resulting assignment is a functor after each morphism group is quotiented by the relation identifying a map with its negative; before that quotient the sign is not canonical.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot cobordism in $S^3\times[0,1]$, the ordinary even integral Khovanov assignment has source and target the bigraded groups $Kh^{i,j}$ and is defined up to an overall sign; after quotienting morphisms by sign, it is invariant under ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary and respects composition. If the surface is equipped with a dividing set and one $w$- and one $z$-basepoint on each boundary knot, the decorated knot Floer assignment has source and target the filtered complexes $CFL^-_{UV}(S^3,K)$ over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$, and is invariant up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. For a general gluing of decorated four-dimensional cobordisms, the link Floer composition law sums over Spin-c structures on the composite that restrict to the chosen structures on the pieces; for the product $S^3\times[0,1]$ this sum has one term. The two assignments therefore have separately specified targets, coefficient rings, decorations, and equivalence relations.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ be the Frobenius algebra with unit $\eta(1)=1$ and multiplication $m$. In the algebraic TQFT, consider the movie that first creates a disjoint circle and then attaches a saddle band merging that circle with one existing circle. The induced local map is
$$
\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\eta} \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\xrightarrow{m}\mathcal A,
$$
and this composite is the identity on $\mathcal A$.

The diagram records the two successive surface events; it is only a description of the movie, while the verification below is algebraic.

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta}"]
& \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "m"]
& \mathcal A
\end{tikzcd}
```

current_clause.heading: Statement refuted
current_clause.text:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ with unit $\eta(1)=1$ and counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$. On a movie with one unaffected circle, birth a disjoint circle and then cap that same circle by a death. The composite operator is
$$
\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\eta} \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}\otimes\epsilon} \mathcal A,
$$
which is zero and therefore is not the identity, even after allowing multiplication by an overall sign.

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta}"]
& \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
\arrow[r, "{\operatorname{id}\otimes\epsilon}"]
& \mathcal A
\end{tikzcd}
```

The movie is a cylinder on the original circle disjoint union a born-and-capped sphere; the diagram specifies the local birth and death sequence and is not used as a proof.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface, with product collars and boundary the finite oriented links $-L_0$ and $L_1$ in the two ends. Components of $S$ and either boundary link may be empty. After an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller prescribed end collars, $S$ has a finite movie consisting of planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves R1, R2 and R3, births, oriented saddle band moves, and deaths. All exceptional times are distinct. The movie's actual smoothly embedded trace is ambient isotopic to the given $S$ relative to those collars, with its boundary orientations and parametrizations retained. Prescribed regular endpoint diagrams may be retained. This is movie existence; it asserts no equivalence theorem for two movies.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text:
Assume countable choice and put $R=\mathbb F_2[U,V]$. The following principle applies to free $R$-modules with specified bases and $R$-linear maps whose matrix coefficients count finite sets, each point carrying a weight $(a,b)\in\mathbb N^2$ and contributing $U^aV^b$. Require finite support for every input basis vector, so these are polynomial maps, not unspecified infinite sums. Suppose that for each input, output and total weight there is an actual compact smooth one-manifold whose boundary is in a specified weight-preserving bijection with the disjoint union of the products of counted sets occurring in an asserted identity. Product weights are the sums of the two factor weights. Additional boundary points are allowed only when equipped with a weight-preserving fixed-point-free involution. Then that identity, with every displayed term added over $\mathbb F_2$, holds coefficientwise.

In particular the principle proves $d^2=0$ when the unpaired boundary is exactly the twice-broken count defining $d^2$; proves $d_BF+Fd_A=0$ when the unpaired boundary is exactly those two broken types; and proves $F_1+F_0=d_BH+Hd_A$ when the boundary is exactly those four types. With three complexes it proves $F_{12}+F_2F_1=d_CH+Hd_A$ under the corresponding four-type boundary description. These are, respectively, the square-zero, chain-map, chain-homotopy and composition-up-to-homotopy identities. The statement assumes the actual compact manifolds, finiteness and exact boundary bijections; it supplies no analytic regularity, compactification, gluing, exhaustion or naturality theorem.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Fix $\infty\in S^3$, put $A=\{\infty\}\times[0,1]$, and identify its complement with $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$. Let $S_0,S_1$ be compact smooth oriented link cobordisms disjoint from $A$, with the same fixed boundary parametrizations and product collars. If they are ambient isotopic in $S^3\times[0,1]$ relative to those collars, then their comparison factors into finitely many ambient isotopies supported in the Euclidean complement and finitely many local sheet passages through $A$. Each sheet passage occurs at a regular surface-height point and gives the sweep-around move: in planar movies, a closing arc for a one-interval tangle travels over the tangle to the opposite side and returns underneath, or the inverse, retaining its orientation. All end collars remain fixed. No assertion that a sweep-around is generated by the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito moves, or that any homology map respects it, is made.

current_clause.heading: Definition
current_clause.text:
Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold, and let $L\subset Y$ be a nonempty finite oriented link with finite disjoint sets of marked points $\mathbf w,\mathbf z$ alternating on each component, with at least one point of each type on each component. Write $n=|\mathbf w|=|\mathbf z|$. An embedded multipointed Heegaard diagram consists of a genus-$g$ oriented surface $S$ splitting $Y$ into handlebodies, $g+n-1$ disjoint compressing curves of each type $\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta$, their actual pairwise-disjoint compressing disks, and the points $\mathbf w,\mathbf z$ off the curves. Each disk system cuts its handlebody into $n$ balls, each containing one boundary-parallel link arc joining one $w$-point to one $z$-point. The two systems of arcs together are the prescribed $L$; the matching permutations may have several cycles. Curves of opposite types meet transversely in finitely many points. Orient $S$ as the boundary of the $\alpha$-handlebody. For disconnected $Y$ with every component meeting $L$, take one such diagram on each of its finitely many connected components. A doubly pointed knot diagram is the case $n=1$; the existing multipointed knot convention is the case in which the arc matchings form one cycle in $S^3$.

Put $d=g+n-1$ and use $\operatorname{Sym}^{d}(S)$ and its product tori $\mathbb T_{\boldsymbol\alpha},\mathbb T_{\boldsymbol\beta}$ on a connected component. For $d=0$ the symmetric product and the two empty products are one point. Intersection generators are finite: each is a choice of one of the finitely many intersections for each curve, with a permutation matching the two curve systems. Include the generator-to-Spin-c labelling $\mathfrak s_w$ furnished by the chosen compatible Morse vector fields as part of the specified diagram data. The underlying module in a fixed label $\mathfrak t$ is the free module on its generators; this definition does not assert that the labels are independent of choices.

A coloring is a map $\sigma:\mathbf w\sqcup\mathbf z\to P$ to a specified finite set, with coefficient ring $R_P=\mathbb F_2[X_p:p\in P]$. A disk or polygon class with nonnegative marked multiplicities is assigned the monomial $\prod_{w\in\mathbf w}X_{\sigma(w)}^{n_w}\prod_{z\in\mathbf z}X_{\sigma(z)}^{n_z}$. The two-color specialization sends every $w$-variable to $U$ and every $z$-variable to $V$, giving $R=\mathbb F_2[U,V]$. On disconnected diagrams use the tensor product of the component modules over this same specified ring and the tuple of their Spin-c labels. These are the underlying modules and weights for intermediate links in a decorated cobordism decomposition. An actual differential, its finite counts, square-zero or curvature identity, and comparison maps require their separate analytic and naturality proofs; no such property is part of this module definition.

current_clause.heading: Definition
current_clause.text:
Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Let two finite generic planar movies represent compact smooth oriented surfaces in $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$, with the same parametrized boundary and product collars. If their embedded surfaces are ambient isotopic with compact support relative to those collars, then the two movies are related by a finite sequence of the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito local types, distant interchanges of disjoint elementary movie events, and planar isotopies. All orientations and omitted-coordinate crossing orders are retained. This statement concerns Euclidean isotopies; it supplies no sweep-around relation.

current_clause.heading: Definition
current_clause.text:
Fix a based closed disk $D$ and a finite even subset $B\subset\partial D$. A smoothing is a compact smooth one-manifold in $D$, with boundary precisely $B$ and fixed radial collars there; it may contain circles. A morphism from $P$ to $Q$ is a compact orientable, not separately oriented, smooth surface with corners in $D\times[0,1]$, with bottom $P$, top $Q$, side boundary $B\times[0,1]$ and fixed product collars. Identify surfaces by ambient isotopy relative to these boundary collars. Take free abelian morphism groups, compose by stacking, and impose the following relations in every surrounding surface: a sphere component is zero; a torus component may be deleted with factor $2$; and $C_{12}+C_{34}=C_{13}+C_{24}$, where $C_{ij}$ attaches a tube between disk patches $i,j$ among four disjoint patches in a ball. Denote the resulting category by $\mathcal C(B)$.

For a surface $C$ set $\deg C=\chi(C)-|B|/2$. Permit formal shifts $P\{a\}$, with a surface of degree $e$ having degree $e+b-a$ as a map $P\{a\}\to Q\{b\}$. Take finite direct sums with matrices of morphisms. A complex is a bounded cochain complex in this additive category, whose differential has internal degree zero. A chain map has cochain degree zero; all homotopies have cochain degree $-1$. Unless specified otherwise, maps and homotopies have internal degree zero. Two chain maps are homotopic when $f-g=dh+hd$. Write $K(B)$ for the category with these complexes as objects and chain maps modulo homotopy as morphisms. Call a complex simple if its invertible endomorphisms in $K(B)$ of internal degree zero are exactly the two maps $\pm\operatorname{id}$ (allowing coincidence when the object is zero).

A planar template is a disk with finitely many numbered input disks removed and a properly embedded one-manifold of arcs and circles in the remainder, meeting each boundary in its prescribed marked points. It acts on smoothings by insertion, and on surfaces by insertion in the template crossed with $[0,1]$. Extend by multilinearity to finite sums. For ordered complexes $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ its totalization has term $\bigoplus_{r_1+\cdots+r_s=r}D(C_1^{r_1},\ldots,C_s^{r_s})$, with shifts added, and differential $\sum_i(-1)^{r_1+\cdots+r_{i-1}}D(1,\ldots,d_i,\ldots,1)$ on that summand. For homogeneous maps $f_i$ of cochain degrees $a_i$, use the sign $(-1)^{\sum_i a_i\sum_{j<i}r_j}$ on $D(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$, evaluated on the input summand of degrees $(r_j)$; this is the usual tensor sign convention, independently of the internal grading.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category, let $P$ be a smoothing consisting of $k$ arcs and no circles, including $k=0$. The map $\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{End}^0(P)$ sending $n$ to $n\operatorname{id}_P$ is an isomorphism of rings. Consequently the one-term complex $P$, with any common grading shift, is simple.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: In the open Bar-Natan categories, planar totalization defines operations on bounded complexes and on their homotopy categories, preserving internal degrees and homotopy equivalences. Simplicity is invariant under an internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalence. In particular let $A$ and $B$ be the operations of adjoining a fixed boundary crossing complex and its proposed inverse, each using precisely two adjacent boundary legs. Suppose local internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences of their two possible composites with the straight two-strand identity complex have been supplied. Then a complex $C$ is simple if and only if $A(C)$ is simple. This is a conditional assertion about these local inverse equivalences; it does not assert Reidemeister invariance or provide crossing complexes or their inverse maps.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category on four boundary points of a rectangle, let $I$ be the vertical two-strand identity pairing and let $E$ be the pairing consisting of a top cap and bottom cup. Let $t:I\to E$ and $s:E\to I$ be the elementary saddle surfaces. Define the formal crossing complexes $K_+=(I\{1\}\xrightarrow{t}E\{2\})$, in cochain degrees $0,1$, and $K_-=(E\{-2\}\xrightarrow{s}I\{-1\})$, in degrees $-1,0$. Then both planar stackings $K_+K_-$ and $K_-K_+$ have explicit internal degree zero strong deformation retractions onto the one-term complex $I$ in degree zero, with no grading shift. All maps and homotopies can be inserted into an arbitrary planar surrounding complex. Consequently adjoining either of these crossing complexes preserves simplicity in both directions.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Let $P$ be a single arc in a disk and let $Z=P\sqcup O$ add a small disjoint circle next to it. Let $m:Z\to P$ merge the circle into the arc by an elementary saddle and let $\Delta:P\to Z$ be the reversed saddle. In the open Bar-Natan category the two normalized kink complexes $C_+=(Z\{1\}\xrightarrow{m}P\{2\})$ in cochain degrees $0,1$, and $C_-=(P\{-2\}\xrightarrow{\Delta}Z\{-1\})$ in degrees $-1,0$, both have explicit internal degree zero strong deformation retractions onto the one-term complex $P$ in degree zero. These retractions are preserved by insertion into an arbitrary planar surrounding complex.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Assume countable choice. Assign to births, deaths and saddles their elementary formal surfaces, and to the Reidemeister kink, inverse-crossing and third-move constructions the explicit formal retractions specified below. Then the two sides of each Euclidean Morse movie relation MM11, MM12, MM13, MM14 and MM15 induce chain maps equal up to an overall sign. This includes both directions, reflected models, all compatible orientations, and insertion into a fixed planar surrounding complex. It asserts the five Morse movie identities for those choices; it asserts no spherical sweep-around identity.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text: Let $f:U\to V$ be an internal degree zero chain map between bounded cochain complexes in the additive open Bar-Natan category. Define $T(f)^n=U^n\oplus V^{n-1}$ and $D_f=\begin{pmatrix}d_U&0\\f&-d_V\end{pmatrix}$. Suppose chain maps $i:Q\to U$, $p:U\to Q$ and $h:U^n\to U^{n-1}$ have internal degree zero and satisfy $pi=1_Q$, $1_U-ip=d_Uh+hd_U$, $hi=ph=h^2=0$. Then $T(f)$ strongly retracts onto $T(fi)$ by the explicit block maps given below. Likewise, if $i:Q\to V$, $p:V\to Q$ and $h:V^n\to V^{n-1}$ satisfy the corresponding equations on $V$, then $T(f)$ strongly retracts onto $T(pf)$. All block maps and homotopies have internal degree zero; no abelian-category or exactness assumption is needed.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text:
Assume countable choice. Put six points on a disk boundary in clockwise order $1,2,3,4,5,6$, at northwest, northeast, east, southeast, southwest and west. Consider diagonal arcs $a$ from $1$ to $4$ and $b$ from $2$ to $5$, and an arc $c$ from $6$ to $3$. In the left diagram $c$ bows above the intersection of $a,b$; in the right it bows below. In both diagrams $c$ passes over both diagonals. Either $a$ passes over $b$ in both diagrams, or $b$ passes over $a$ in both. These are the two local third Reidemeister variants considered here. More precisely one can use the diameters $y=-x,y=x$ for $a,b$ and the curves $y=\pm h(1-x^2)$, $0<h<1/2$, for $c$, with fixed radial collars near the six boundary points.

Use the local smoothing chart in which the over-strand joins southwest to northeast and the under-strand joins northwest to southeast. The A-smoothing joins the top pair and bottom pair, and the B-smoothing joins the left pair and right pair. An A-first cube uses $0=A,1=B$; a B-first cube uses $0=B,1=A$. For either convention, the raw formal cube of an ordered diagram has term $\bigoplus_{|v|=s}S_v\{s\}$ in cochain degree $s$ and edge saddle coefficient $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$ in coordinate $j$. For any choice of strand orientations, put this term in degree $s-n_-$ and shift it internally by the additional $n_+-2n_-$.

For each of these two smoothing conventions, the formal cubes of the two diagrams admit internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences, with explicit maps given below. The displayed smoothing table and cone calculation use B-first cubes: turning right from an entering underpassing half-line gives the B-smoothing. The A-first maps are obtained from the raw B-first maps by complementing every bit and reversing surface time, without spatial reflection, with the explicit vertex sign correction below; only after this operation are the same given $n_+,n_-$ normalizations applied to both sides. All these maps and homotopies can be inserted into any planar surrounding complex.

current_clause.heading: Statement
current_clause.text:
Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg1=1$, $\deg X=-1$, and structure maps $m,\eta,\Delta,\epsilon$ given by $\eta(1)=1$, $\epsilon(1)=0$, $\epsilon(X)=1$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, and $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. There is an additive symmetric monoidal functor $F$ from the category of closed Bar-Natan smoothing cobordisms before local relations to finite free graded abelian groups. Here closed means that objects consist of circles, including the empty collection, and there are no vertical side intervals. The target has all integral linear maps, graded by their homogeneous degrees, and its symmetry is the ordinary interchange of tensor factors, without a Koszul sign from quantum degrees.

Explicitly, $F(C)$ is the free group on the labelings of the finite circle set of $C$ by $1,X$, graded by the sum of the label degrees. For a connected surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$, with $p$ incoming and $q$ outgoing circles, its map in any temporary ordering of those circles is $F(\Sigma)=\Delta_q H^g m_p$, where $H=m\Delta$, $m_0=\eta$, $m_1=1_{\mathcal A}$, $m_p$ is iterated multiplication for $p\ge2$, $\Delta_0=\epsilon$, $\Delta_1=1_{\mathcal A}$ and $\Delta_q$ is iterated comultiplication for $q\ge2$. For a disconnected surface, take the tensor product over its connected components and route each factor to its actual boundary circle. The empty surface is sent to $1_{\mathbb Z}$. This construction is independent of all temporary orderings, respects embedded isotopy, stacking and disjoint union, sends the elementary birth, death, merge and split to $\eta,\epsilon,m,\Delta$, and sends a surface to a homogeneous map of degree $\chi(\Sigma)$. It respects S, T and four-tube and therefore descends to the closed Bar-Natan quotient category.
